standard_prerequisites.name: Kummer theory: a degree p Galois extension of a field containing a primitive p-th root of unity is obtained by adjoining the p-th root of an element of the base field
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the element b whose p-th root generates M over L, which is the input to every case distinction in the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Weakly unramified extensions go up along a totally ramified extension, so the integral closure in the compositum remains weakly unramified over the new base
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the compositum of the chosen totally ramified extension with the given towers again has the weak unramifiedness required of the conclusion.

standard_prerequisites.name: The pre-purely-inseparable case: if the residue class of the unit is not a p-th power then the extension of discrete valuation rings is weakly unramified
standard_prerequisites.use: Disposes of the case in which the residue class of the unit is not a p-th power, which is one of the two alternatives in the conclusion.

core_obligations: Fix a uniformizer pi of A and apply Kummer theory to write M as L adjoined the p-th root of an element b of L (proof lines 35102-35105).

Treat the case where the order of b at the valuation of B is prime to p: choose a degree p separable extension K_1 over K totally ramified with respect to A, let A_1 be the integral closure, observe that the integral closure B_1 of B in the compositum is a discrete valuation ring weakly unramified over A_1, and record what happens when K_1 over K is not a weak solution (proof lines 35107-35116).

In the remaining case, reduce to the situation where b is pi^n times a unit with n divisible by p, so that M is obtained from L by adjoining the p-th root of a unit, replacing the base by the totally ramified extension when necessary (proof lines 35117-35124).

For a unit u whose residue class is not a p-th power, conclude that the extension of discrete valuation rings is weakly unramified by the pre-purely-inseparable case; otherwise replace the chosen root y by y over v where v^p and u have the same residue class so that y^p equals 1 plus pi times an element of B (proof lines 35126-35136).

In that last situation identify the extension as a degree p extension of finite level with the explicit element xi equal to pi b over w^p, which is the second alternative of the conclusion (proof lines 35137-35139).
proof_roadmap: Use Kummer theory to obtain the element whose p-th root generates M over L (proof lines 35102-35105).
If its order is prime to p, build a totally ramified degree p extension and use weak unramifiedness going up along it (proof lines 35107-35116).

After replacing the base, reduce to a unit and split into the case where its residue class is not a p-th power, which is weakly unramified, and the case where it is, which gives finite level (proof lines 35117-35139).
difficulty_reason: The statement concerns a tower A inside B inside C of discrete valuation rings with A of mixed characteristic, A to B weakly unramified, B containing a primitive p-th root of unity and the top extension Galois of degree p, and concludes the existence of a finite Galois extension of K, totally ramified over A, that either is a weak solution for the tower or makes the top extension one of finite level (statement lines 35087-35100). The proof is a case analysis driven by Kummer theory and by the order of the element whose p-th root generates the top extension: in the case where that order is prime to p a totally ramified degree p extension is built so that the compositum has the required weak unramifiedness, and in the remaining case the base is replaced so as to reduce to a unit, after which either the residue class is not a p-th power and weak unramifiedness follows from the pre-purely-inseparable case, or the equation can be brought to the form y^p = 1 + pi b, which exhibits finite level with an explicit element (proof lines 35102-35139). Both alternatives of the conclusion are produced by explicit constructions. The counted span refers four times, three of them to earlier results of this chapter and one to Kummer theory in another chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.
